01_foundations/09_alter_table.title: Altering database records
01_foundations/09_alter_table.description: Add a phone_number column to the customers table.
hints: Use ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN
The column needs a name and data type
Use VARCHAR(20) for phone numbers

01_foundations/11_phone_formatting.title: Format phone numbers
01_foundations/11_phone_formatting.description: The customers table has been pre-loaded with 8 customer records (IDs 1-8). Add a phone_number column, then set phone numbers: customer 5 gets '1234567890', customer 6 gets '123-456-7890', customer 7 gets '(987)654-3210', customer 8 gets '9876543210'.
hints: ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN phone_number VARCHAR(20)
Use UPDATE with CASE based on customer_id
Phone numbers are intentionally stored in different formats

01_foundations/08_insert_records.title: Inserting database records
01_foundations/08_insert_records.description: The customers table exists but is empty. Insert 5 customer records of your choice. Each customer needs: firstname, lastname, username, password, email, and created_on.
hints: Use INSERT INTO customers (columns) VALUES (values)
Add CURRENT_TIMESTAMP for created_on
Include all required columns in the INSERT

01_foundations/03_string_functions.title: String Functions
01_foundations/03_string_functions.description: Format user names: show username in uppercase, email in lowercase, and the length of their bio.
hints: Use UPPER() for the username
Use LOWER() for the email
Use LENGTH() for the bio character count
Use aliases with AS for clean column names

01_foundations/02_order_limit.title: ORDER BY and LIMIT
01_foundations/02_order_limit.description: List the top 3 most expensive products by price, from highest to lowest.
hints: Use ORDER BY price DESC
Add LIMIT 3 to get only the top 3
SELECT product_name and price

01_foundations/10_delete_records.title: Deleting database records
01_foundations/10_delete_records.description: The customers table has been pre-loaded with records including two customers with lastname 'Smith'. Delete all customers whose lastname is 'Smith', then the remaining customers should be: Alison Riesher, Charlie Brown, Diana Lee.
hints: Use DELETE FROM customers
Use WHERE to target only Smith entries
Verify with SELECT before deleting

01_foundations/06_group_by_having.title: GROUP BY with HAVING
01_foundations/06_group_by_having.description: Find departments that have at least 2 employees and a total salary budget exceeding $150,000. Show department, headcount, and total salary.
hints: Use GROUP BY department
Use COUNT(*) for headcount
Use SUM(salary) for total salary
Use HAVING to filter after grouping

01_foundations/01_select_where.title: SELECT with WHERE
01_foundations/01_select_where.description: Query employees who earn more than $60,000 in the Engineering department.
hints: Use WHERE salary > 60000
Add AND department = 'Engineering'
SELECT only first_name, last_name, and salary

01_foundations/05_aggregate_basics.title: Aggregate Basics
01_foundations/05_aggregate_basics.description: Calculate total revenue, average order value, number of orders, and the highest single order for each month in 2024.
hints: Use SUM(total) for total revenue
Use AVG(total) for average order value
Use COUNT(*) for number of orders
Use MAX(total) for highest single order
Use EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) or DATE_TRUNC for grouping

01_foundations/00_create_table.title: Creating a table
01_foundations/00_create_table.description: Create the customers table from scratch. Include columns: customer_id (SERIAL PRIMARY KEY), firstname, lastname, username, password, email (all VARCHAR NOT NULL), and created_on (TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP).
hints: Use CREATE TABLE with column definitions
Add SERIAL PRIMARY KEY for customer_id
Include password as a VARCHAR column between username and email

01_foundations/07_union_set.title: Set Operations (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT)
01_foundations/07_union_set.description: You have two tables: active_users and archived_users. Find all email addresses that appear in BOTH tables (INTERSECT), and also find emails that are in active_users but NOT in archived_users (EXCEPT).
hints: Use INTERSECT to find common emails
Use EXCEPT to find emails only in active
Both SELECT statements must return the same number of columns
No need for ORDER BY

01_foundations/04_date_functions.title: Date Functions
01_foundations/04_date_functions.description: Find all projects that were overdue as of April 1, 2025 and show how many days overdue they were.
hints: Use CURRENT_DATE to get today's date
Use end_date < CURRENT_DATE to find overdue projects
Use CURRENT_DATE - end_date to get days overdue
Filter out projects with NULL end_date

05_window/02_rank_dense.title: RANK and DENSE_RANK
05_window/02_rank_dense.description: Rank employees by salary within each department. Show RANK and DENSE_RANK side by side so you can see the difference when salaries tie.
hints: RANK() leaves gaps after ties (1,1,3,4)
DENSE_RANK() does not leave gaps (1,1,2,3)
Add a tie by making two employees have the same salary in one department

05_window/03_ntile.title: NTILE
05_window/03_ntile.description: Divide employees into 4 quartiles based on salary across the whole company. Show name, salary, and which quartile they fall into (1 = highest, 4 = lowest).
hints: NTILE(4) divides the ordered rows into 4 buckets
ORDER BY salary DESC so quartile 1 has highest salaries
No PARTITION BY needed — this is company-wide

05_window/06_frames.title: Window Frames and Running Totals
05_window/06_frames.description: Calculate a running total of sales per month, plus a 3-month moving average. Show month, monthly_sales, running_total, and moving_avg_3mo.
hints: For running total: SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)
For 3-month moving average: AVG(amount) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
Use DATE_TRUNC('month', sale_date) for monthly aggregation first

05_window/05_first_last_value.title: FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE
05_window/05_first_last_value.description: For each employee, show their salary compared to the highest and lowest salary in their department. Use FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE with window frames.
hints: FIRST_VALUE(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) gives the highest
LAST_VALUE needs a frame: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
Without the frame, LAST_VALUE only sees up to the current row

05_window/01_row_number.title: ROW_NUMBER
05_window/01_row_number.description: Assign a sequential number to each order per customer, ordered by order_date descending (most recent = 1). Show customer name, order date, total, and the row number.
hints: PARTITION BY customer_id to restart numbering per customer
ORDER BY order_date DESC for most recent first
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC)

05_window/04_lag_lead.title: LAG and LEAD
05_window/04_lag_lead.description: For each employee, show their salary alongside the previous employee's salary (by hire date) and the next employee's salary. Also show the difference from the previous salary.
hints: LAG(salary) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) gets previous row's salary
LEAD(salary) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) gets next row's salary
LAG(salary, 1, 0) uses 0 as default when there's no previous row

09_leetcode/05_tree_traversal.title: Tree Traversal with Recursive CTE
09_leetcode/05_tree_traversal.description: Given a 'nodes' table where each node has a parent_id (NULL for root), classify each node as 'Root' (no parent), 'Inner' (has both parent and children), or 'Leaf' (has parent but no children).
hints: Use a recursive CTE to find all ancestors/descendants
Or use simpler approach with subqueries: check p_id IS NULL for Root
Check EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nodes WHERE parent_id = n.id) for Inner vs Leaf

09_leetcode/04_median.title: Median Calculation
09_leetcode/04_median.description: Find the median salary for each department. Use percentile_cont or a combination of ROW_NUMBER and COUNT to compute the median.
hints: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) computes the median directly
Use it as a window function: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department)
SELECT DISTINCT if using window functions to avoid duplicates

09_leetcode/03_stadium.title: Human Traffic of Stadium
09_leetcode/03_stadium.description: Find records where there are 3 or more consecutive rows with `people >= 100`. Show visit_date and people for those rows.
hints: Use LAG and LEAD to compare consecutive rows
A row is part of a consecutive group if it OR its neighbors have people >= 100 in a chain of 3
Alternative: subtract row_number from some grouping value to form groups

09_leetcode/02_consecutive.title: Consecutive Numbers
09_leetcode/02_consecutive.description: Find all numbers that appear at least 3 times consecutively in the Logs table. Use the LAG and LEAD window functions.
hints: Use LAG(num, 1) and LAG(num, 2) to look back at previous rows
Filter WHERE num = LAG(num, 1) OVER (ORDER BY id) AND num = LAG(num, 2) OVER (ORDER BY id)
SELECT DISTINCT num to avoid duplicates

09_leetcode/01_department_top3.title: Department Top Three Salaries
09_leetcode/01_department_top3.description: Find employees who earn the top three salaries in each department. If fewer than 3 employees in a department, return them all. Show department, employee name, and salary.
hints: Use DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC)
DENSE_RANK handles ties correctly (ties share the same rank)
Filter WHERE rank <= 3 in an outer query

06_specialties/03_fulltext.title: Full-Text Search
06_specialties/03_fulltext.description: Implement full-text search on a blog_posts table. Find posts that match the query 'database performance tuning' using tsvector and tsquery. Show title, rank, and a highlighted snippet.
hints: Use to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || body) to create the search vector
Use plainto_tsquery('english', 'database performance tuning') for the query
Use ts_rank() to order by relevance
Use ts_headline() to show highlighted matches

06_specialties/04_enums.title: Enum Types
06_specialties/04_enums.description: Create and use a custom ENUM type for order statuses. Then query to find all orders with statuses that are NOT 'delivered' or 'cancelled' (i.e., active orders).
hints: CREATE TYPE order_status AS ENUM('pending', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled')
Use the enum type as a column type in the orders table
Filter with WHERE status NOT IN ('delivered', 'cancelled')

06_specialties/05_type_casting.title: Type Casting and Formatting
06_specialties/05_type_casting.description: You have a table with messy data: dates stored as strings, prices as text with dollar signs, and phone numbers in inconsistent formats. Clean and transform each column into proper types.
hints: Use ::DATE to cast strings to proper date type
Use REPLACE to remove $ then ::NUMERIC
Use REGEXP_REPLACE for phone number formatting
TO_CHAR for output formatting

06_specialties/06_password_encryption.title: Encrypt passwords in users table
06_specialties/06_password_encryption.description: Create a users table with plain-text passwords and explore encryption with pgcrypto.
hints: CREATE TABLE users with user_id, username, password
Enable the pgcrypto extension with CREATE EXTENSION
Use crypt() and gen_salt() to hash passwords

06_specialties/01_jsonb.title: JSONB Operations
06_specialties/01_jsonb.description: Query a table with JSONB data. Find all products where the metadata contains a color field, and extract specific fields from the JSONB into separate columns.
hints: Use -> to get JSONB field as JSON, ->> to get as text
Use @> containment operator or ? key-existence operator
Example: metadata @> '{"color": "red"}'::jsonb
Project: metadata->>'color' AS color

06_specialties/00_create_user.title: Creating a new read-only user
06_specialties/00_create_user.description: Create a new database user named 'readonly_user' with a password, then grant them SELECT-only access on the customers table.
hints: Use CREATE USER ... WITH PASSWORD
GRANT SELECT ON customers TO readonly_user
The user can read but not modify data

06_specialties/02_arrays.title: Array Operations
06_specialties/02_arrays.description: Work with PostgreSQL arrays. Find all employees who have 'Python' in their skills array, show their name, and the total number of skills they have.
hints: Use ANY() or @> to check array containment
Use array_length(skills, 1) for count of skills
Use ARRAY['Python', 'SQL']::varchar[] or '{Python,SQL}'::varchar[] syntax

03_aggregation/02_having.title: HAVING Clause
03_aggregation/02_having.description: Find departments where the average salary is above $60,000 and there are at least 3 employees.
hints: GROUP BY department
HAVING AVG(salary) > 60000 AND COUNT(*) >= 3
AVG(salary) filters groups after aggregation

03_aggregation/03_rollup_cube.title: ROLLUP and CUBE
03_aggregation/03_rollup_cube.description: Using ROLLUP, generate total sales grouped by (year, quarter) with subtotals per year and a grand total. Also try CUBE.
hints: Use GROUP BY ROLLUP(year, quarter)
EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) for year
EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM order_date) for quarter
ROLLUP adds subtotals for each level of grouping

03_aggregation/00_duplicates.title: CREATE bookmarks table & find duplicates
03_aggregation/00_duplicates.description: Create a bookmarks table, insert data including intentional duplicates, then identify them.
hints: CREATE TABLE with id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, url, name, description
Some URLs appear more than once in the INSERT
Use GROUP BY with COUNT to find the duplicate URL

03_aggregation/04_filtered_agg.title: Filtered Aggregates
03_aggregation/04_filtered_agg.description: For each month in 2024, show total sales, and break out sales by region (North, South, East, West) in separate columns using FILTER.
hints: Use FILTER (WHERE region = 'North') inside each aggregate
DATE_TRUNC('month', sale_date) for month grouping
Example: SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE region = 'North') AS north_sales

03_aggregation/01_group_basics.title: GROUP BY Basics
03_aggregation/01_group_basics.description: For each product category, find the total stock, average price, cheapest product price, and most expensive product price.
hints: GROUP BY category
SUM(stock), AVG(price), MIN(price), MAX(price)
ROUND(AVG(price), 2) for clean decimals

03_aggregation/05_case_aggregation.title: Conditional Aggregation with CASE
03_aggregation/05_case_aggregation.description: Create a summary showing how many students got each letter grade (A: >=90, B: >=80, C: >=70, D: >=60, F: <60) for each course. Show course name and count per grade.
hints: Use CASE inside COUNT() for each grade bucket
CASE WHEN score >= 90 THEN 1 END counts A's
GROUP BY course_id, course_name

08_expert/02_isolation_levels.title: Transaction Isolation Levels
08_expert/02_isolation_levels.description: Demonstrate the difference between READ COMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ isolation levels. The query should return the current balance from the accounts table using SERIALIZABLE isolation.
hints: Use BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE;
SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE account_id = 1;
Then COMMIT;
Different isolation levels affect what dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantom reads are possible

08_expert/01_recursive_cte.title: Recursive CTE
08_expert/01_recursive_cte.description: Using a recursive CTE, generate the organizational hierarchy starting from the CEO (manager_id IS NULL). Show employee name, level (depth), and the path from CEO to employee.
hints: Anchor: SELECT employee_id, name, 0 AS level, name::TEXT AS path WHERE manager_id IS NULL
Recursive: JOIN employees ON manager_id = anchor.employee_id, increment level
Append to path with path || ' -> ' || e.name
Use UNION ALL between anchor and recursive members

08_expert/05_partial_index.title: Partial and Expression Indexes
08_expert/05_partial_index.description: Create a partial index on orders for only 'pending' status orders. Then create an expression index on LOWER(email) in the customers table. Query using both indexes.
hints: Partial index: CREATE INDEX idx_pending_orders ON orders(status) WHERE status = 'pending'
Expression index: CREATE INDEX idx_lower_email ON customers(LOWER(email))
Query must use the same expression: WHERE LOWER(email) = 'alice@example.com'
The partial index is only used when WHERE matches the condition

08_expert/04_explain_analyze.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
08_expert/04_explain_analyze.description: First create an index on the orders(customer_id) column. Then run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a query that joins customers with orders. The output should show an Index Scan being used.
hints: CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer ON orders(customer_id)
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT ... JOIN orders ON customer_id ...
The plan should show 'Index Scan' or 'Bitmap Index Scan' using the created index

08_expert/06_row_level_security.title: Row-Level Security
08_expert/06_row_level_security.description: Implement Row-Level Security (RLS) on the 'documents' table. Each user should only see their own documents. Enable RLS, create a policy, and query as a specific user.
hints: ALTER TABLE documents ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
CREATE POLICY user_documents ON documents USING (owner = current_user)
Create a test user and grant SELECT on the table
SET ROLE test_user; SELECT * FROM documents; RESET ROLE;

08_expert/03_for_update.title: FOR UPDATE and SKIP LOCKED
08_expert/03_for_update.description: Select the next available (unlocked) job from a queue using SKIP LOCKED. Mark it as 'in_progress' by updating its status, and return the job details.
hints: BEGIN the transaction first
SELECT ... FROM jobs WHERE status = 'pending' ORDER BY created_at FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1
UPDATE jobs SET status = 'in_progress' WHERE job_id = ...
Then COMMIT
SKIP LOCKED skips rows locked by other transactions

07_plpgsql/02_param_function.title: Function with Parameters
07_plpgsql/02_param_function.description: Create a function 'get_products_by_price_range(min_price NUMERIC, max_price NUMERIC)' that returns all products within a price range (inclusive).
hints: Use RETURNS TABLE(product_id INT, name VARCHAR, price NUMERIC)
RETURN QUERY SELECT ... WHERE price BETWEEN min_price AND max_price
Use LANGUAGE plpgsql

07_plpgsql/03_set_returning.title: Set-Returning Function
07_plpgsql/03_set_returning.description: Create a function 'get_department_summary()' that returns a table with department, employee_count, total_salary, and avg_salary for each department.
hints: Use RETURNS TABLE(department VARCHAR, employee_count BIGINT, ...)
RETURN QUERY SELECT department, COUNT(*), SUM(salary), AVG(salary) GROUP BY department
Call the function with SELECT * FROM get_department_summary()

07_plpgsql/05_trigger.title: Triggers
07_plpgsql/05_trigger.description: Create an audit trigger that logs all changes to the 'employees' table. When salary is updated, insert a record into 'salary_audit' with the old and new salary.
hints: Create salary_audit table first (audit_id, employee_id, old_salary, new_salary, changed_at)
Create a trigger function that uses OLD and NEW to access old/new values
CREATE TRIGGER AFTER UPDATE OF salary ON employees FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION ...

07_plpgsql/04_stored_procedure.title: Stored Procedure
07_plpgsql/04_stored_procedure.description: Create a stored procedure 'transfer_product_stock(from_product_id INT, to_product_id INT, qty INT)' that transfers stock between products. It should decrement quantity from the source and increment on the destination, and raise an exception if insufficient stock.
hints: Use CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE (not FUNCTION)
Use LANGUAGE plpgsql
Check stock with IF (SELECT quantity FROM products WHERE product_id = from_id) < qty THEN RAISE
Use UPDATE for both products inside a single transaction

07_plpgsql/01_basic_function.title: Basic PL/pgSQL Function
07_plpgsql/01_basic_function.description: Create a PL/pgSQL function called 'total_orders_for_customer(p_customer_id INT)' that returns the total number of orders for a given customer. Then call it with customer_id = 1.
hints: Use CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION
Function returns INTEGER
Use LANGUAGE plpgsql
Use SELECT COUNT(*) INTO result FROM orders WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id

02_joins/05_anti_join.title: Anti-Join
02_joins/05_anti_join.description: Find customers who have NEVER placed an order. Use three different techniques: LEFT JOIN + IS NULL, NOT IN, and NOT EXISTS. Results should be the same.
hints: Technique 1: LEFT JOIN orders ON ... WHERE order_id IS NULL
Technique 2: WHERE customer_id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL)
Technique 3: WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id)

02_joins/04_multi_join.title: Multi-Table JOIN
02_joins/04_multi_join.description: Show each order with the product name, quantity, the customer who placed it, and the salesperson who handled it.
hints: Join orders -> customers, orders -> order_items, order_items -> products, orders -> salesperson
Use meaningful table aliases (o, c, oi, p, s)
You'll need 4 tables joined together

02_joins/03_self_join.title: Self JOIN
02_joins/03_self_join.description: Find pairs of employees who work in the same department. Show each pair once (e.g. 'Alice Johnson' and 'Bob Smith' but not the reverse). Exclude pairing an employee with themself.
hints: Join the employees table to itself
Use aliases e1 and e2
Condition: e1.department = e2.department AND e1.employee_id < e2.employee_id
The < avoids duplicates and self-pairings

02_joins/01_inner_join.title: INNER JOIN
02_joins/01_inner_join.description: List each order with the customer's full name and email. Only include orders that belong to existing customers.
hints: Use INNER JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id
Use CONCAT(first_name, ' ', last_name) or || for full name
SELECT order_id, full_name, email, total

02_joins/02_left_right_join.title: LEFT and RIGHT JOIN
02_joins/02_left_right_join.description: Show all customers and their orders, including customers who have never placed an order. Include customer name and total (NULL if no orders).
hints: Use LEFT JOIN to keep all customers
LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id
Orders without customers will show NULL values

04_subqueries/02_derived_table.title: Derived Table (Subquery in FROM)
04_subqueries/02_derived_table.description: Find the top 3 highest-paid employees per department. Use a derived table with ROW_NUMBER() to rank employees within each department.
hints: First create a derived table with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC)
Then in the outer query, filter WHERE rn <= 3
The derived table goes in the FROM clause as a subquery

04_subqueries/03_exists_in.title: Subqueries with EXISTS / IN
04_subqueries/03_exists_in.description: Find all customers who have placed an order with a total greater than $200. Use both IN and EXISTS approaches (separate queries, but for verification just provide one).
hints: IN: WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE total > 200)
EXISTS: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE customer_id = c.customer_id AND total > 200)
EXISTS is usually faster for large datasets

04_subqueries/04_cte.title: Common Table Expressions (CTE)
04_subqueries/04_cte.description: Using WITH (CTE), write a query that finds the top 2 products by total revenue (quantity * price) for each category. Use a CTE to compute product revenue, then ROW_NUMBER to rank within categories.
hints: Start with WITH product_revenue AS (SELECT ...)
Compute quantity * price as revenue, join order_items with products
Then use a second CTE or subquery for ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ...)

04_subqueries/05_correlated.title: Correlated Subqueries
04_subqueries/05_correlated.description: Find employees who earn more than the average salary of their department. Show employee name, department, their salary, and the department average. Order by salary descending.
hints: A correlated subquery references the outer query's table
SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.department = e1.department
Use this subquery in the WHERE clause: salary > (subquery)
Also include it in SELECT to show the department average

04_subqueries/01_scalar_subquery.title: Scalar Subquery
04_subqueries/01_scalar_subquery.description: Show each employee's name, salary, and how their salary compares to the department average. Include columns: name, department, salary, dept_avg_salary, and salary_diff (salary - dept_avg).
hints: Use a correlated scalar subquery in SELECT to compute AVG(salary) for the employee's department
The subquery needs a WHERE clause matching the department
Salary diff can be computed as salary - subquery_result

04_subqueries/00_address_cte.title: Query addresses
04_subqueries/00_address_cte.description: The orders table has been pre-loaded with 10 records. Add street, city, state, zip_code columns. Then use a CTE with address data to populate: order 3 gets '123 Main Street, Springfield , CA, 12345', order 4 gets '234 Elm Avenue, lexington, ky, 23456', and so on for orders 6-10. Note the inconsistent formatting (extra spaces, mixed case, zip+4).
hints: ALTER TABLE to add all four address columns
Use WITH address_data AS (VALUES ...) CTE
UPDATE orders FROM address_data to populate the new columns
